page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8559C processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and 2 threads per core operating at 3.2 GHz. The CPU includes a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions). The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 2500 GB NVMe SSD. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2314.0 placing it in the top tier (top 10%). Single-threaded gzip compression (34.74 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.0 GB/sec) also demonstrate strong performance. However, multi-core performance is more limited due to the 2-core physical layout; the stress-ng multi-core score of 4390.57 and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression score of 28.2 GB/sec fall into the weak category. Memory bandwidth is mixed, with read-only large block bandwidth at a weak 34.18 GB/sec, while write large block bandwidth reaches an average 36.32 GB/sec. Redis SET operations are weak at 6.09 million operations per second, but static web serving throughput is average at 8.21 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the i7ie.xlarge offers high local storage density and DDR5 memory capacity relative to its 4 vCPUs, making it a specialized option for storage-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. The inclusion of AMX instructions enables average performance for small to medium LLM inference tasks, such as prompt processing for 7B models at 35.14 tokens per second. This hardware profile is best suited for databases, local-storage-heavy applications, text processing, and lightweight web serving where high single-core speed and large local NVMe storage are prioritized over multi-core scaling.
